A warm welcome from Mr David Massiah, the Head Teacher of London Christian School
Welcome to LCS Welcome to London Christian School
Who are we ? A look inside LCS
LCS is like the perfect village school but in the heart of London. Timeless values that set a child up for life coupled with a top 21st century curriculum. And the amazing school staff are the ones who make it happen; supported by parents who really care about their kids.
Leaders provide an inclusive and supportive school culture through a curriculum which encourages pupils to respect and care for others and develop an understanding of their own identity.
Teachers utilise their good subject knowledge to create well-planned lessons that incorporate a breadth of activities aimed at developing independence and enabling good progress. Resources are used effectively, ensuring they are suitable for the pupils’ ages and aptitudes.

Our pupils
Our pupils are our greatest testament to the education we provide.
With a healthy mix of teacher input and independent learning, pupils are encouraged to express their creativity and understanding in a variety of different ways such as writing, speaking, art, music, dance, drama, sport and technology.
Christian ethos
We believe that every area of school life should be informed and distinctively shaped by our Christian foundation, and by an ethos that is kind, academically ambitious, full of co-curricular opportunities and which encourages each child to think for themselves and to serve others. Children of all faiths and none are warmly welcome.
Encourage and develop
From a non-selective intake we achieve the best results for your child to progress to their next choice of school.
We are not only about preparing for these assessments. We encourage excellent learning habits throughout each child’s school life. From the moment your child arrives, we aim to find out their strengths and gifts (academic or otherwise) and to encourage and develop these.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Aims & Values | Private Primary School London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
​We exist to provide an excellent Christian education for children in London.
Our vision
We will develop your child as an individual within a nurturing environment shaped by our Christian ethos that is kind, academically ambitious, full of co-curricular opportunities and which encourages each child to think for themselves and to serve others.
Christian ethos
We believe that every area of school life should be informed and distinctively shaped by our Christian foundation. Your child will be taught the Christian faith and witness it lived out within our community. Children of all faith backgrounds are warmly welcome. Your child will be encouraged to explore, develop and share their own beliefs and values in an open, respectful environment.
Develop
Whatever their starting point, our aim is for your child to reach their full potential.
Individual
We treat everyone as an individual with their own strengths and needs. We help each child to achieve academic excellence and to grow in their unique personality.
Kind
We believe that these five values, rooted in a Christian understanding of the world and human nature, play a significant role in the development of character. Kindness is the pervading atmosphere in which your child will be immersed.
The expectation will be that they give as well as receive kindness in word and deed. Staff will embody kindness in their interactions with your child and with each other.
We also teach our children what respect is and how to live it out.
Academically ambitious
From a non-selective intake we achieve the best results for your child to progress to their next choice of school.
We are not only about preparing for these assessments. We encourage excellent learning habits throughout each child’s school life. From the moment your child arrives, we aim to find out their strengths and gifts (academic or otherwise) and to encourage and develop these.
Co-curricular opportunities
We offer a range of opportunities designed to expand the personal development of your child including taking advantage of our central London location, extra curricular clubs, sporting activities and use of technology.
Think for themselves
We take time to ensure each child understands the knowledge they receive so that they can make up their own minds and use information wisely and creatively.
Serve
We encourage every child to develop an awareness of the interests of others. This is closely linked to kindness, but we will create opportunities for all ages to serve the school and wider community.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Independent Primary School London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to London Christian School
We are an independent primary school that exists to provide an excellent Christian education for children in London.
​London Christian School was established in September 2007 and started with just 4 pupils. Since then the school has flourished to its current size of 120 pupils across eight classes, aged from 3 to 11 years old.
​We encourage pupils to develop their own talents and personality and we value diversity in our school community.
​Our carefully crafted curriculum is built around a traditional Biblical Christian understanding of the world and human nature, and pupils learn in a nurturing environment in which they feel safe and happy. Class sizes are kept small so that the curriculum can be differentiated to the needs of each child, allowing them to grow both socially and academically.
​We hope that you will enjoy finding out about our school. Please contact us to arrange a private tour. We look forward to meeting you.
David Massiah Head Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: School Life | Independent Primary School London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
Why Choose London Christian School?
Stimulating Curriculum
Our curriculum combines a rigorous academic focus with an engaging, creative approach. We adapt units of work to each student’s interests and abilities, ensuring that they make exceptional progress.
Purposefully tailored activities form a stimulating and lively learning environment and we use art, drama and music throughout the curriculum to inspire the imagination and develop creative skills.
We organise regular school trips to complement the curriculum. Students visit the Greenwich Observatory, British Museum and Houses of Parliament, as well as a variety of theatres and galleries.
Personalised Teaching
We keep class sizes small so that each student can be challenged in line with his or her abilities and has frequent opportunities for one-to-one tuition with teachers and teaching assistants. Small class sizes also contribute to a loving, caring environment. Withdrawal groups ensure that students receive extra input where they need it, whether that is through More Able extension work or additional support.
Holistic Approach
We believe children make the best academic progress when they are happy and safe. The atmosphere of the school is intimate and friendly, with capacity for about 120 children. Our carefully designed Personal, Social and Health and Economic Education (PSHE) programme teaches social skills and emotional awareness.
Christian Ethos
We teach and model values that have stood the test of time. This helps us establish a loving atmosphere and close community within the school. All our class teachers are committed Christians, and every area of school life is informed by and built on our Christian foundation. We are delighted to welcome children from any background, regardless of religion or belief.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years Curriculum | Christian Schools in London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
The educational programme is planned with reference to the Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage and the Development Matters in the Early Years Foundation Stage guidance material that supports practitioners in implementing the requirements of the EYFS.
Prime areas of learning and development are:
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Specific areas of learning and development are:
Running through all of these areas of learning are the characteristics of learning; playing and exploring, active learning, creating and thinking critically.
Every day is filled with fun and lively activities spread across the breadth of our curriculum. Each term or half term, we have a theme or topic which navigates us through our learning. Examples are Traditional Tales, Under the Sea, Minibeasts, Seasons, People Who Help Us and Growing. We aim to follow the children’s interests and adapt topics accordingly.
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World
Expressive Arts and Design

pageCache.pageTitle: Years 1-6 Curriculum | Waterloo | London Christian School
pageCache.text: The starting point of our planning is the Primary National Curriculum. From this framework we have built our own programme, linking topics where we can and ensuring that pupils are ready for the 11+ and for secondary school learning. It is a privilege to be able to add a unique London Christian School feel to our lessons.

This week, Year 3 have been practising maths in practical ways. Post-it note number lines keep appearing all over the floor in the hall! We’ve used place value counters to partition 3-digit numbers. Maths has been coming alive and we can’t wait to see what we learn next!

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Christian Primary Schools in London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
Excellent pastoral care underpins our teaching and all of school life. It is essential to confident and joyful learning. We are a small school in which the children are known and cared for as individuals.
The Deputy Head oversees and plays a central role in pastoral care at LCS. Here are some of the ways in which we ensure that we look after individuals well.
PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic) lessons with the class teacher each week.
Pupil voice is heard through the School Council which surveys pupils on matters such as bullying as well as organising theme days in which all the children can express something of their culture, heritage, creativity and interests.
The children are given regular formal opportunities to feed back their views and feelings about areas such as playtimes, friendships, feeling safe and what they love most about school.
Each class from Years 1 to 6 has a “worry box” in which the children are encouraged to express (anonymously if they wish), things that are troubling them.
Parents know their children well, and we keep lines of communication open with parents and know how important it is to work in partnership in the pastoral care of each child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governance | Independent School London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
Our Governing Body consists of current and past parents, staff members and external individuals, all with a passion for seeking to develop our school. They meet each half term to discuss the school action plan and to monitor safeguarding, finances and implementation of policies. Our Governors are keen to be involved in school life through visits, assemblies and events.

pageCache.pageTitle: After School Clubs | Christian Schools in London | London Christian School
pageCache.text:
Activity Clubs allow pupils to be cared for after school while enjoying an enriching variety of activities such as art, digital literacy, sport, acting, and singing. The programme for Activity Clubs is set at the beginning of the year and provides opportunities for a wide variety of pursuits catering for small groups of pupils and designed to cater specifically to the age range of the pupils. Activity clubs run after school every day until 4:30pm (5pm on Fridays) and each club makes use of the expertise and interests of our staff team or visiting staff. Activity Clubs run on a yearly basis and are payable for the entire academic year. Sign up will be available during the summer prior to the start of the Autumn Term.
Every Day Club provides after school care consistent with the standards and ethos of our school. It runs after school every day until 5.30pm. For Year 1-6, Everyday club includes supervised Homework Club from 4:30-5:30pm.
Art
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Drawing, sketching, painting, fine motor skill development
DESCRIPTION: Art clubs provide an opportunity to develop creativity, artistic skill and techniques. Pupils will spend time using different types of media and produce pieces of art work throughout the year.
Enquire about our Art Club
Ballet
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Sense of rhythm, posture, agility, musicality, stamina
DESCRIPTION: Ballet provides a fun atmosphere to develop self-confidence, poise, stamina, co-ordination and musicality with our RAD qualified tutor. Ballet shoes are required and specific uniform is compulsory from Year 1 onwards, as pupils work towards exams. Please see the Ballet Uniform page for more details.
Enquire about our Ballet Club
Craft
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Craft techniques, fine and gross motor skills, interpretation and creativity
DESCRIPTION: Craft club will introduce an engaging variety of art and craft styles and techniques to to encourage creativity and experimentation with different materials and mediums. Pupils will work on craft pieces to take home and display proudly.
Enquire about our Craft Club
Digital
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Digital literacy, logic, programming, e-safety
DESCRIPTION: Digital club provides an exciting opportunity to develop digital literacy and logic skills within a safe setting using school approved software. Pupils will be introduced to the world of computer programming at an age appropriate level.
Enquire about our Digital Club
Drama
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Eloquence, speech and drama, expression, improvisation, performance
DESCRIPTION: This club is for budding performers and will focus on developing confidence through speech and drama. Pupils will learn about voice projection, expression, gesture, stage position and movement.
Enquire about our Drama Club
Eco
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: To care for and understand the impact that humans have on the environment; fine and gross motor skills
DESCRIPTION: Eco club will involve activities which explore nature on our doorstep. Pupils will develop cutting skills, cooking, creating smaller crafts and will do some litter picking. They will also do some upcycling projects.
Enquire about our Eco Club
Music
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Understanding pitch, developing rhythm, musical theory, creativity
DESCRIPTION: This club will develop students’ musicality, rhythm and listening skills in the context of playing tuned percussion and through musical games and activities. It will involve some elements of music theory to increase technical understanding.
Enquire about our Music Club
Sports
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Fitness, agility, ball skills, co-ordination, sportsmanship
DESCRIPTION: This club will teach focused skills in an age-appropriate context of team games including football, basketball and rugby. Lessons will focus on improving ball skills, co-ordination, fitness and agility. Skills are applied to modified games for the development of sportsmanship and learning team strategy.
Enquire about our Sports Club
Tutoring
SKILL DEVELOPMENT: Numeracy, verbal and non-verbal reasoning, comprehension
DESCRIPTION: If considered appropriate in conjunction with your child’s class teacher, pupils can practise and develop skills in Literacy and Maths with a highly experienced tutor, in a group setting.
